**W1203 bounded Paperless question lookup (2026-09-25):**
POST /api/paperless/consult requires its own paperless:consult:read scope and a
strict question/limit body. It captures the accepted instance configuration;
requests cannot choose a vault/subdirectory. The new no-follow reader bounds
questions to4KiB, results to20, enumeration to1000entries, each document to256KiB
and total reads to8MiB. A genuinely absent directory returns empty; malformed,
unreadable, linked or over-budget data returns a fixed503. Blocking disk work
uses spawn_blocking. Responses expose filename/score/excerpt, never internal paths.
Shared legacy scoring retains full-string Unicode lowercase semantics and now
maps match positions back to original UTF-8 boundaries; both expanding lowercase
and Greek final-sigma regressions cover the change. Review also corrected the
cap-std timestamp conversion and an explicit Option type before publication.

Captured the exact branch via `#[cfg(test)]` DIAG markers: the risk-confirm single-use consume's `rename(leases.json.tmp → leases.json)` hits a Windows AV/indexer sharing-violation that outlasts 50ms → `consume_risk_leases` fail-closes → no `RISK_CONFIRM_USED` frame → `verdict=""`. Widened `retry_transient_io` to ~2s (20 attempts, linear backoff capped 150ms); fail-closed preserved, Unix no-op. Verified: dispatch green ×16 consecutive direct test-exe runs (it failed on run 1 pre-widen). Windows-local FS flake (Unix-CI parallel + Windows `--test-threads=1` CI don't hit it); also hardens prod — a valid risk-confirm lease no longer fails-closed on an AV hiccup.
>
> **Follow-up 2 (2026-06-29):** a 4th flake surfaced in the same hunt — `cluster::registry::tests::concurrent_{distinct_peer_upserts,rtt_and_stability_refresh}`. Root cause was lock-ordering, not FS: every registry write path took the OS file lock (`cluster.yaml.lock`) BEFORE the in-process `REGISTRY_LOCK` mutex, so concurrent same-process writers SPIN on the file lock (50ms retry, 5s give-up) instead of PARKING on the mutex — under full-suite CPU saturation the holder starves and the spinners trip the 5s timeout → `upsert`/`refresh` Err → test panic (`held by another process for >5s`). Fixed: swapped all 5 write paths to **mutex-first** (park don't spin; only the mutex-holder touches the file lock; cross-process lost-update protection preserved; consistent order = no deadlock). Windows-local/overload flake; correct structure regardless.

(1) **`Drop` now uses `zeroize::Zeroize`** (volatile writes + `compiler_fence(SeqCst)`), replacing the prior plain `*b = 0` loop that the compiler is free to elide. (2) **Automatic `Clone` removed** — duplicating secret material now goes through the explicit `SecretBytes::clone_for_storage(&self) -> Self` method. (3) **`CredentialEntry.secret: String` field removed** entirely from `security::credential_redact` — the SC-17 redactor never read it, so carrying it through allocated a transient plaintext `String` on the way to /dev/null. `build_import_record` in `credentials/mod.rs` no longer calls `.expose_str().to_string()` on the SecretBytes; the secret stays inside the wizard's `ImportedCredential` and goes directly to the secret-store writer without a parallel allocation. Drift guard added (`credential_entry_carries_no_secret_field`) — a future PR that re-adds `secret: String` to `CredentialEntry` will fail this compile-time check via the explicit struct literal. Two existing tests updated for the new contract: `secret_bytes_clone_for_storage_equals_original_constant_time` (was `_clone_`) + `redactor_drops_name_url_username` (was `_secret`).

### v0.3 — Auto-update (operator wish-list B)

> **Current implementation correction (2026-07-15; supersedes the historical
> Session-25/MV-01b mechanics below):** self-update no longer calls
> `atomic_replace_binary`, exposes `backup_path`, or restores caller-managed
> `*.bak` files. Authenticated archives are closed-extracted and the complete
> compiled release profile is committed by one durable `InstallTransaction`,
> with the locally generated portable-ownership marker before the public core.
> A running Windows portable CLI uses a signed target-binary PID handoff and
> emits `0xD2` only after the child transaction commits. Registered Inno,
> native Linux DEB/RPM, and signed macOS App layouts fail closed; selecting and
> executing their exact signed platform installer/package is still open under
> `GOLD-R4-02` and must not be inferred as complete from the historical rows.

The boxed `Fn() -> Vec<ComponentSpec>` builder runs ON each tick so a transient network failure becomes a Failed outcome instead of crashing the daemon. **`tokio::task::spawn_blocking` + `std::panic::catch_unwind`** isolates builder panics — a misbehaving probe never aborts the loop. Per tick: emit `0x44 UPDATER_TASK_FIRED` BEFORE the pass (audit chain proves the cron started even when the daemon is killed mid-pass) → run_updater_pass → emit `0x45 UPDATER_TASK_RESULT` with the full payload. `run_updater_tick` is the pure-fn helper tests use to exercise the WAL emit + builder composition without spinning up the full loop. 5 tests: default-config-pinned / interval-clamp-60s / interval-uses-configured-above-floor / tick-emits-both-frames / spawn-None-when-disabled / spawn-Some-when-enabled (immediate abort so ticker doesn't fire). (2) `save_session_card(home, ts_unix, prompt, reply)` builds a 2-turn transcript (operator + agent), runs `compress_session`, persists via the existing atomic save_card path. (3) `save_session_card_best_effort(...)` swallows IO errors → warn-log so the chat exit never fails on a hindsight write. (5) `next_session_seed_banner(home, current_session_id)` renders `"[neoth] last session: <one_line_summary>"` with built-in guards: no prior card → empty, current_session_id matches latest → empty (suppresses same-second self-loop). ## v0.9 — Proactivity + Slave coupling + Native PC control + Arxiv + killer features

### v0.9 — Proactivity (full from operator wish-list G)

- [x] **G-01** Self-initiated message engine — pattern-detection cron emits "I noticed X, want me to do Y?" via operator-preferred channel. Drains `G-01a ProactiveQueue`. — 4d — 🔧 **CHANNEL-DELIVERY ADAPTER SHIPPED 2026-05-29 Session 28d (4-lens senior-dev gremium: architecture / ops-reliability / security-privacy / NEOTH-idiom).** Verify-first corrected the scope: the producer (`ProactiveQueue` + G-01-mini reflection cron + G-02 surfacer) AND the consumer drain (`daemon/proactive_dispatcher.rs` → `proactive_delivered.jsonl` sidecar) were ALREADY shipped + wired in serve.rs. The ONLY open gap was the last link — nothing actually SENT a drained item to the operator's channel; it only hit the JSONL ledger. That's the slice this closes. **Gremium consensus → design:** (1) ARCHITECTURE — FOLD the send into the drain tick (no separate sidecar-tailing task; no cadence mismatch to decouple, avoids double-bookkeeping); send happens BEFORE `queue.save_to` so a mid-send crash re-drains next tick = at-least-once, `dedup_key` bounds duplicate harm. (2) RELIABILITY — one send attempt per item; outcome recorded as `delivered`/`failed`/`suppressed`/`sidecar_only` in BOTH the JSONL ledger (new `append_delivery_records` writes the `status` per line — fixes the old "unconditional delivered" footgun) AND a WAL frame; NEVER re-enqueue a failure (would starve the 3/day budget). Fixed by decoupling the blocking read into a **dedicated reader thread** that feeds an `mpsc` channel; `request_board` now waits on `recv_timeout(5s)` instead of an unbounded `read_line`, so a stalled daemon can neither pin the per-tick worker nor delay teardown past the timeout (→ cold fallback + reconnect). The related HIGH ("panic wedges in-flight forever") + the `stdin.take()` orphan + the SQLITE_BUSY race + the "init_tracing stdout corrupts protocol" + the "ADV-15 autonomy=None bypass" were all **refuted** with code-grounded reasoning (no reachable panic in the worker body; unreachable `take()` None branch; checkpoint-PRAGMA returns a row not an error; `NEOTH_LOG=error` + the named error sites unreachable in the subprocess; no production caller constructs a daemon-origin config without `.with_autonomy()`).

### v1.0 — Hermes adopts (clarify + goal)

- [x] **CL-01** Clarify-prompt interrupt — mid-turn open question via SSE, 120s timeout. — 2.5d (hermes adopt) ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-06-03 Session 36 (panel rank-9, verify-first reasoned closure — same root cause as GM-01).** CL-01's interactive 'interrupt before the provider call, ask the operator, wait 120s for an answer, resume' is an ARCHITECTURAL MISMATCH with NEOTH's model: `cli/chat.rs:8` is explicit — **'No interactive REPL'** + 'single-turn chat reply'. `neoth chat "prompt"` is ONE-SHOT (the operator passed the prompt + isn't sitting at a TTY) — a blocking `ask_clarify_cli` stdin-read would HANG a one-shot command waiting for an answer that never comes (a bug, not a feature). The channel/serve path handles each inbound INDEPENDENTLY (no stateful mid-turn pause/resume) — the operator's 'answer' arrives as a SEPARATE inbound, not a resumption; building pause/resume is a deep stateful refactor. The only NEOTH-fitting alternative (a deterministic keyword ambiguity classifier → inject an 'ask-for-clarification' system-prompt nudge) is MARGINAL: the LLM already asks for clarification on ambiguous/under-specified requests natively (a keyword heuristic is a weaker duplicate of model judgment) and it costs 8-site EnrichmentInputs churn for behaviour the model already exhibits. **PREREQUISITE for a real CL-01 (tracked):** an interactive `neoth chat` REPL (no-prompt-arg → stdin loop) OR a stateful channel mid-turn-pause/resume layer — only then is the clarify-interrupt a genuine consumer. **Systemic finding: hermes-adopts (GM-01, CL-01) assume an agentic multi-turn loop NEOTH deliberately doesn't have for chat; verify-first closes them honestly instead of building primitive-ahead/harmful code.**
- [x] **GM-01** Goal manager + turn budget — self-terminate when goal satisfied. — 3d (hermes adopt) ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-06-03 Session 36 (panel rank-8, verify-first).** The TURN-BUDGET half is now operator-tunable + the GOAL-SATISFACTION half is closed as an architectural mismatch. **Verify-first found:** NEOTH chat is single-turn request-response (no agentic multi-turn session to 'self-terminate'), and the ONE real iterative loop (MCP autoroute `dispatch_loop::run_tool_loop`) ALREADY had a turn budget (`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS=5` + `hit_cap`). A keyword-overlap 'goal satisfied' heuristic wired into that tool-loop would risk PREMATURE task termination → harmful, not helpful → NOT built (would be primitive-ahead + dangerous). **Shipped (the genuine deliverable):** the dispatch-loop cap is now operator-tunable via `freedom.yaml::goal.max_turns` (new `GoalConfig`, default 5 = no behaviour change) — threaded `run_mcp_dispatch_loop`→`run_tool_loop_with_cap` on BOTH the `neoth chat` + channel-serve paths (via `PipelineHandlerDeps.goal_max_turns`). 1 config test (default-5 / absent-block / explicit). lib 6792/0, clippy 0. The hermes 'goal manager + classify_goal_satisfaction' stays unbuilt by design (mismatch with NEOTH's request-response model; the coding-workflow already has its own `EarlyStopDetector`).

## Sequencing rules (carry-over + new from A2)

1. **Each lane ships independently.** v0.2.1 hotfix MUST tag before any v0.3 work merges. v0.3 must tag and be public-ready before v0.4 work starts on `main`.
2. **WAL frame band reservations** — claim event-type IDs in this file BEFORE implementation. v0.3 claims `0x11`, `0x12 extend`, `0x15`, `0x80..83`, `0x05/06`. v0.4 claims `0x30`. v0.9 claims `0x19/1A`, `0x50/51`, `0x60`, `0x78/79`, `0x94`, `0xA4/A5/A6`, `0xE8`. v1.0 claims final cleanup band. Coordinate via this file before any new WAL event lands.
3. **Wizard is the activation surface for every lane.** Every new operator-facing feature ships with a wizard step + a settings-panel entry (GUI ↔ CLI parity hard rule).
4. **Security blockers are pre-merge.** PC-02 Chrome DevTools MCP requires env-var force + license confirm BEFORE the PR opens, not in v1.0 hardening. CRIT-01/02/03 from A5 must ship in v0.2.1 hotfix lane BEFORE any v0.3 work merges.
5. **A2 critical sequencing dependencies:**
   - W-05 (installer trait) ships before U-01/U-03
   - M-07 (memory tests) → M-09 (region routing) → OM-01 (OMI ingest)
   - P-01+P-02 (approval tiers) → PC-01 (OS tool surface) — sonst brutale confirm fatigue
   - G-01 with `G-01a ProactiveQueue` → PL-03 / OB-03 — sonst notification storm
   - OB-01 (dreaming→vault) → G-01 (trigger) → N-06 (workflow delivery)
   - W-03 with `operator_complexity_level()` → GU-03 (panel collapse rule engine)
   - AR-05 `neoth profile conflicts` → G-02 (proactive surfacing wrong claims)
6. **No "next-version" debt creep.** Items deferred from a lane move to the explicit `_post-v1.0_` column above, not silently into the next lane.

## How to use this file

- Pick the highest-priority lane that's not yet shipped.
- Pick an item from the top of that lane's section.
- Flip `[ ]` → `[~]` in the same commit you start work.
- Ship code + tests + same-turn `[~]` → `[x]` flip with commit hash + 1-line evidence.
- Push.
- Repeat.

### Audit-RPC strict V2 supersession (2026-07-28)

The historical AUDIT-RPC-01 entry above records the original loopback-TCP
delivery, but that transport is no longer the current contract. R3-17 replaces
it with kernel-authenticated same-user OS IPC: an owner-private Unix socket or
current-user-only Windows named pipe, discovered through the strict bounded
`~/.neoth/audit_rpc.endpoint.v2.json` record. There is no TCP fallback, port
advertisement, or token hint; the per-boot bearer remains defense in depth.

- [x] **GOLD-COMPANION-P2P-01** Companion v2 server-side pairing preview over HyperDHT + authenticated Noise-IK P2P — ✅ DONE: `daemon/companion.rs` announces a topic through HyperDHT and admits only the topic-and-PSK-HKDF-derived expected client static key before transport allocation; the encrypted application-level constant-time 16B PSK check remains defense in depth. After admission, its typed owner drains bounded leave, WAL `0x0D` audit acknowledgement, in-memory token visibility, and reply rather than abandoning the task at startup, TTL, or shutdown. The audit deliberately contains no bearer token: a crash after its ACK but before visibility consumes the invite fail-closed and requires a new invite/pairing; it is not a crash-recoverable token transaction. `CompanionInvite::from_hex` emits v2 `neoth://companion/pair?v=2` URLs; WAL `0x0D COMPANION_P2P_PAIRED` + `0x0E COMPANION_P2P_REJECTED` remain in `wal/events.rs` + EVENT_NAME_TABLE entries + band-guard assertions; `CompanionConfig.p2p_enabled: bool` is in `config/automation.rs`; `cli/companion.rs` runs the listener; `cli/mod.rs` dispatches `.await`; `cli/serve_tasks.rs` owns the serve-side invite-file poll coordinator and ordered drain after the companion HTTP drain; `cli/serve.rs` hoists `companion_p2p_state` and wires `BackgroundHandles`; `docs/cli-commands.md` is generated.   **Zwei echte Produktdefekte gefunden, beide still, beide Windows-only:**
  1. **Audit-RPC bediente EINE Verbindung pro Daemon-Lebenszeit** (`72e93437`). `run_accept_loop` wartet auf `accept()` in einem `tokio::select!`; das Future wird verworfen, sobald der andere Zweig gewinnt — und `accept()` entnahm die pending Named-Pipe-Instanz **vor** dem `connect()`-await. Ein Abbruch zerstörte damit die einzige lauschende Instanz, der Loop behandelt jeden Accept-Fehler als fatal. Unsichtbar, weil `AuditSink::DaemonRpc` per AUDIT-RPC-01 best-effort ist. Unix nie betroffen (hält per Referenz, `UnixListener::accept` ist cancel-sicher) → Linux-CI konnte es nicht sehen.
  2. **DACL-Vergleich gegen `GENERIC_ALL`** (`4c023a25`), den Windows nie zurückliefert → jeder Bind scheiterte, ebenfalls still.
  **Ein Produktdefekt in der Logik:** der Tonfall-Klassifikator hob sich selbst auf — `"correct"` traf in „in**correct**", `-0.5 + 0.5 = 0.0`. Die expliziteste Korrekturformulierung war die einzige, die nicht erkannt wurde (`d3f061b2`, Wortgrenzen + 2 Regressionstests).
  **Ein Budget-Defekt:** der Loader belastete `.neoth-skills.lock` dem Eintrags-Budget des Operators (`e01bb728`).
  **Messfehler bei mir selbst:** minimaler PATH ohne PowerShell blähte die Zahl um 2 auf; `SRC/_gate_min.bat` hat denselben Mangel.
  ★★★ **Muster über alle ~28 Fixes:** fast jede Fixture brach, weil sie einen **exakten Satz oder ein exaktes Layout** festnagelte statt der Invariante. Der Code wurde jeweils *besser* — präzisere Fehlermeldung, stärkere Liveness-Prüfung (gehaltenes Lock statt bloßer PID), gehashte Operator-ID statt Klartext, zusätzlicher Audit-Marker — und die Tests meldeten die Verbesserung als Regression. Beim `cli::chat`-Fall hätte ein „Fix" die Datenschutz-Härtung zurückgedreht.
